# Tendkit

> Customer support you own: a shared inbox, tickets and a customer portal that you copy into your own app with the shadcn CLI. Customer emails, WhatsApp and SMS become tickets your team answers next to the customer's account. MIT licensed.

Tendkit targets Next.js (App Router), Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query and Drizzle (Postgres, or SQLite/Cloudflare D1). Channel adapters use only fetch and WebCrypto, so they run on Cloudflare Workers, Node, Bun and Deno.

## Install

`npx shadcn@latest add https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-postgres.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/support-ui.json https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/channel-resend.json`

Registry items: support (core), support-postgres, support-d1, support-ai (optional AI engine), support-ai-postgres, support-ai-d1, support-ui, channel-resend, channel-microsoft365, channel-gmail, channel-smtp, channel-twilio, channel-whatsapp, channel-telegram, channel-api. Each is at https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/r/<item>.json.

## How to integrate (for coding agents)

1. Install the items above with the shadcn CLI (server items into the API package, support-ui into the web app in a monorepo).
2. Export the support schema from the Drizzle schema and generate a migration. Don't apply migrations without asking.
3. Create the service with createSupport({ store, storage, channels, directory, notify, acknowledgement, fromName, portalChannelId, ignoreFrom, team, teamEmail, replyAll }).
4. Implement the SupportDirectory: identify (sender to user and customer/account), searchCustomers, getCustomers, listAgents. This is the only product-specific part.
5. Route POST /api/webhooks/support/[channel] to support().handleWebhook(channel, request). Call support().runScheduled() from a cron every few minutes.
6. Expose the agent methods (listTickets, getTicket, reply, addNote, assign, setStatus, linkCustomer, changeContact, uploadAttachment, attachmentUrl, counts, listAgents, searchCustomers) and support().portal through the app's own API behind its own auth; implement SupportClient with them and render SupportInbox/SupportTicket inside SupportProvider.
7. Optional AI (triage, one-line summaries, suggested replies; agents review and send, except on topics the team switches to Autopilot): add support-ai-postgres or support-ai-d1, export the ai-schema and migrate, then pass ai: supportAi({ model, store: createPostgresAiStore(db), knowledge: [docsFromUrl("https://…/llms-full.txt")], defer }) to createSupport. model is any Vercel AI SDK LanguageModel; Tendkit imports only the "ai" package. Add describeCustomer(customerId) to the directory for account facts. For a product translated when its docs aren't, pass interfaceLabels: (language) => ({ "Get Verified": "Se faire vérifier", ... }) | null; labelsFromMessages(en, fr, { exclude? }) from knowledge builds it from i18n files, and each prompt gets only the labels it mentions, so replies name screens and buttons as the customer sees them. Expose support().ai (refine, writeUp, translate, draft, discardSuggestion, setInsight, getSettings, updateSettings, syncKnowledge, listKnowledgeSources) and put the same methods under ai on the SupportClient; map the inbox's sort: "priority" to listTickets. Customer messages go to the configured model provider. Voice in the reply box (one microphone button; an empty box takes spoken notes through writeUp, a box with text takes a spoken change through refine, or "Insert as spoken" for plain dictation; Escape cancels, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles, two-minute limit): pass transcriptionModel (any AI SDK TranscriptionModel) and optionally transcriptionOptions: ({ language }) => providerOptions to supportAi, expose support().ai.transcribe({ audio, language? }) => { text, language } (audio is a Blob, Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer up to 10 MB, never stored) and add the optional transcribe({ audio: Blob }) to client.ai. Without client.ai.transcribe the screens use the browser's Web Speech API in the SupportProvider locale; with neither the button is hidden. A transcription model is more accurate for languages such as Arabic and French. When the browser listens, it uses SupportProvider's speechLocale (default: locale); pass a region such as "fr-FR" when the UI locale is bare "fr". Memory (needs the 0002_memory migration; every client method is optional and the screens hide what's missing): approved answers are the drafts' most trusted source, cited as { type: "answer" }, and agents insert one by typing "/" at the start of a line in the reply box, with {name}, {company} and {agent} filled in and no model call. Expose support().ai.listApprovedAnswers(), generaliseAnswer({ ticketId, text }) => { title, text, language } (takes the customer's details out of a reply for review), saveApprovedAnswer({ id?, title, text, language?, ticketId?, gapId?, actorId }), deleteApprovedAnswer(id), listGuidanceSuggestions(), decideGuidanceSuggestion({ id, accept, rule?, actorId }), listGaps(), dismissGap({ id, actorId }) and draftArticle({ gapId } | { ticketIds }) => { title, markdown }, and add the same names to client.ai (the client passes { id } objects; the server adds actorId). Drafts an agent edits before sending are kept: the same customer's earlier replies go into that customer's later drafts as they were sent; other customers only ever get a one-sentence style note that is dropped if it holds a digit, link, name from the ticket or five words in a row from the conversation (shareStyleNotes: false keeps every correction within its customer). runScheduled draws those notes on each run and, once a day, proposes guidance rules from heavily edited drafts (never applied until a person accepts) and files unanswered questions (cannot_answer suggestions and discarded drafts) under gaps. supportAi also takes an optional embedder: { embed(texts) => number[][] } to order found corrections by meaning. Actions (needs the 0003_actions migration; every client method is optional): pass actions: [supportAction({ name, title, description, input, approval?, run, available?, timeoutMs? })] to supportAi. name is lowercase letters, digits and underscores; input is a Zod schema, any Standard Schema or the AI SDK's jsonSchema() describing an object; approval is "always" (default: an agent approves every run) or "never" (read-only lookups only); run({ input, ticket, customer, contact, agent, signal }) returns { ok, summary, data? } and is always called with the ticket's own customer, never one the model chose; tickets not linked to a customer have no actions. While drafting, the model may call "never" actions through AI SDK tool calling (up to 6 per draft) and cites each as a source { type: "action", title, detail }. Calling an "always" action from a draft only records a proposal on the suggestion (suggestion.actions: { name, title, input, reason, state: proposed | running | done | failed | declined, fields, run }): nothing a customer writes can run a change. Expose support().ai.ticketActions({ ticketId }) as client.ai.listActions, runAction({ ticketId, action, input, actorId, suggestionId?, text? }) => { run, text } (actorId is the signed-in agent from your server; with suggestionId it approves a proposal once, idempotently; text is the reply box, returned rewritten when the agent changed the inputs), declineAction({ ticketId, suggestionId, action, actorId, text? }) => { text } (the reply rewritten without the action), setActionEnabled({ name, enabled }) (lookups only: stops AI running one on its own; "always" can't be changed from the UI), listActions() (add its result as actions to client.ai.getSettings()) and listActionRuns({ ticketId }). Every run is logged in support_action_runs (approvedBy, input, status: succeeded | failed | timed_out | errored, summary, durationMs) and approved or manual runs add an "action_run" event to the agents' timeline. Runs time out after timeoutMs (default 15000). The screens show proposed actions as cards under the suggested reply (Approve, Skip, editable inputs), ask before sending a reply with undecided proposals, and list available actions in the ticket's menu with a form built from the schema. Autopilot (needs the 0004_autopilot migration, which also backfills topic, language and change on existing support_suggestions; every client method is optional): topics a team switches on are answered with no agent reading first. Nothing is on by default and nothing switches itself on. Track record per topic over windowDays (30): decided drafts split into sent as drafted, lightly edited (editWeight < 0.15: the share of words changed, and at least 0.5 whenever a number, link or email address was added, removed or replaced), rewritten, discarded, came back unhappy (sent as drafted or lightly edited, then the customer's next message was frustrated, angry or said it didn't help) and flagged; plus cannot_answer, sent by Autopilot, reopened, and a split by language. A topic is eligible when its latest minDrafts (30) decided drafts are at least minRate (0.9) sent as drafted or lightly edited and no flagged reply awaits review. Configure with supportAi({ autopilot: { minDrafts, minRate, windowDays, holdMinutes: 10, maxPerHour: 30, blockMoods: ["angry"], blockUrgencies: ["urgent"], maxCustomerMessages: 3, minLanguageDrafts: 5, channels?: string[] (default: every email channel), signature?: false | string | ({ language }) => string, canManage?: (agentId) => boolean } }) or autopilot: false to remove it. The team can only raise minDrafts and minRate from the UI. Expose support().ai.getAutopilot() => { stopped, stoppedBy, stoppedAt, minDrafts, minRate, floor, windowDays, holdMinutes, maxPerHour, sentLastHour, topics: [{ topic, stage: collecting | eligible | on | paused, mode: hold | immediate | null, enabledBy, enabledAt, pausedAt, pauseReason: quality | flagged | null, ready, record }] }, setAutopilotTopic({ topic, on, mode?, actorId }) (switching on or resuming is refused unless the record is eligible; who and when are stored; needs canManage), setAutopilot({ stopped?, minDrafts?, minRate?, actorId }) (the kill switch: any agent can stop, restarting and thresholds need canManage), autopilotExamples({ topic, only?: "changed", limit? }), holdAutopilotReply({ suggestionId, actorId }) and flagAutopilotReply({ suggestionId, actorId, note? }); add the same names to client.ai (the server adds actorId). Modes: "hold" stores the suggestion with autopilot: "held" and sendAt = now + holdMinutes, and runScheduled sends it when due unless an agent stopped it, answered, left a note, changed the status, or the customer wrote again; "immediate" sends as soon as it is drafted. A held reply is claimed atomically (held to sending, one conditional update) before it is sent, stopped, or replaced by an agent's reply, so a customer never gets two; reply() throws "Autopilot has just answered this message" while Autopilot is sending or once it sent the draft the agent started from. A reply is sent only if all hold: the topic is on and Autopilot isn't stopped; the ticket is linked to a customer; the channel is allowed; the model set confident: true, every cited source resolved and at least one is not guidance; no customer message on the ticket reads like an attempt to steer the assistant (looksLikeInjection) and the reply doesn't recite the guidance (either one blocks as not_confident); no action was proposed; mood not in blockMoods and urgency not in blockUrgencies; the customer didn't ask for a person (triage asksForHuman) or say the last reply didn't help (triage notHelped, or came back unhappy after the last suggested reply); fewer than maxCustomerMessages customer messages since the ticket was opened or reopened; the topic has minLanguageDrafts decided drafts in the customer's language at minRate; fewer than maxPerHour sent in the last hour. Otherwise it stays an ordinary suggestion with suggestion.autopilotBlock (stopped, unknown_customer, channel, asked_for_human, not_helped, mood, urgency, long_thread, needs_approval, not_confident, unsourced, language, hourly_cap, held_back, moved_on, send_failed). ai.draft() never sends. A sent reply has authorId null, is signed with fromName and "This reply was sent automatically. If it doesn't help, reply to say so and a person will take over." (never a person's name; left off when the channel has no room), leaves the ticket in "waiting", records suggestion status "used" with autopilot: "sent", and adds an "autopilot_sent" event { messageId, suggestionId, topic, mode } that only agents see. Brakes: flagAutopilotReply pauses the topic (pauseReason "flagged"), reopens the ticket, adds an "autopilot_flagged" event and the question is filed as a gap by the next daily review; a topic whose latest drafts fall under minRate (judged from 10 drafts) pauses with pauseReason "quality", checked before each send and on each runScheduled; setAutopilot({ stopped: true }) stops everything, held replies included. Topic switches live in support_autopilot_topics. The screens: SupportAiSettings shows each topic's readiness, numbers and drafts; the ticket marks the reply "Sent by Autopilot · <topic>" with "Flag as wrong", and shows a held reply with when it goes and "Stop and edit".
8. Insights (a dashboard next to the inbox; needs the 0005_insights migration: three indexes, shipped with the store item, no new tables): expose support().stats({ from, to, responseTargetMinutes? }) => { from, to, previousFrom, responseTargetMinutes, current, previous, days: [{ opened, solved, backlog }], channels: [{ id, kind, address, opened, solved, days }], agents: [{ agent | null, open, waiting, solved, solvedBefore }], customers: [{ customer, tickets, before }], reopened: [{ id, number, subject, at }], late: [{ id, number, subject, waitedMs, answered }] } as the optional client.stats, and render SupportInsights inside SupportProvider. current and previous are { opened, solved, reopened, firstReply: { count, median, p90 }, timeToSolve: { count, median, p90 }, breaches, answered, replies, oneReply }, durations in milliseconds; the previous period has the same length and ends where the chosen one starts. Definitions: time to first reply runs from the customer's first message to the first reply that reached them from an agent or Autopilot (acknowledgements and failed sends don't count; filed under the period the ticket was opened in); time to solve runs from opened to last solved (filed under the period it was solved in); percentiles interpolate linearly (the median of 10, 20, 30, 40 is 25); a breach is a ticket opened in the period whose first reply took longer than responseTargetMinutes or that is open and still waiting past it (wall-clock, no business hours; null without a target); backlog is rebuilt from when tickets were opened and last solved; answered/replies/oneReply describe solved tickets that got a reply; spam is excluded. Nothing is tracked or rolled up: numbers are computed on load through indexes on support_tickets(created_at), support_tickets(solved_at) and support_events(type, created_at), with percentiles ranked in SQL, identically on Postgres and SQLite/D1. Each number links to the inbox, which reads the URL params topic, channel, customer, from, to and status=all and passes ListQuery { topic, channel, customerId, createdFrom, createdTo } with status left out for "all": map them to support().listTickets({ topic, channelId, customerId, createdFrom, createdTo }). SupportProvider takes an optional aiSettingsHref so gaps link to AI settings. With AI (needs the 0006_insights_ai migration: the support_spikes table and an index on support_suggestions(decided_at)): expose support().ai.insights({ from, to }) => { topics: [{ topic, tickets, before, days, drafts, accepted }], urgency: { current, previous }, mood: { current, previous, days }, drafts: { current, previous } each { usedAsIs, lightlyEdited, rewritten, discarded, autopilotSent, autopilotFlagged }, firstReply: { withDraft, withoutDraft }, gaps, spikes } as client.ai.insights (topics, urgency and mood count tickets opened in the period; drafts count those decided in it; accepted means sent as drafted or lightly edited). Spikes: on every runScheduled, a topic raised by at least minCustomers (5) different customers within windowMinutes (120), with at least factor (3) times the tickets the topic usually gets in the same hours of the previous baselineDays (14) days, is recorded in support_spikes and sent once to notify as { type: "insights.spike", spike: { id, topic, startedAt, detectedAt, lastSeenAt, endedAt, tickets, customers, usual, acknowledgedAt, acknowledgedBy } }. Colleagues at one customer count once; contacts without a customer count by contact; the topic "other" never spikes; one ongoing spike per topic (a unique index), its counts updated while it lasts; it ends after a whole window without the detector seeing it. Configure with supportAi({ spikes: { minCustomers, windowMinutes, factor, baselineDays } }) or spikes: false. Expose support().ai.listSpikes({ all? }) (unacknowledged spikes of the last 7 days, each with acknowledgedBy as an agent and latest: its 5 newest tickets) and acknowledgeSpike({ id, actorId }) as client.ai.listSpikes and client.ai.acknowledgeSpike; the inbox and SupportInsights then show an unacknowledged spike as a likely incident with a link to its tickets. support().ai.detectSpikes() runs the check on demand.
9. Proactive and self-serve (starting a conversation needs no AI and no migration; the rest needs AI and the 0007_proactive and 0008_outreach_record migrations: tables support_signals, support_outreach, support_outreach_kinds, support_ask_sessions and a self_serve column on support_ai_settings, then follow_up and the flag columns on support_outreach and pause_reason on support_outreach_kinds; proactive.ts in the core item holds the model-free parts, PROACTIVE_DEFAULTS and SELF_SERVE_DEFAULTS). Start a conversation: support().startTicket({ channelId?, to: { contactId } | { address, name? }, customerId?, cc?, subject?, text, attachmentIds?, agentId }) => { ticket, message } opens a ticket by writing first: status "waiting", assigned to the agent, the person matched to an account through the directory (customerId files a person who isn't linked yet; a person of another customer is refused), sent through the normal send path (the agent's signature on email, Reply-To token, delivery tracking), with a "ticket_started" event and no ticket.created notification or acknowledgement. Replies thread by headers or by the token, and the ticket shows in the customer's portal. channelId defaults to portalChannelId when it can write first, then the first email channel, then the first channel that can; channels with a subject require one; cc is email only, up to 20. If the channel doesn't take the message, the ticket stays with the failed message to retry. Channels declare the optional capability canStartConversation (email adapters and Twilio SMS: true; WhatsApp, Telegram and the signed API channel: false; left out, true when the channel has no reply window and its kind isn't "api"). support().listChannels() => [{ id, kind, address, identityKind, capabilities, startBlockedReason: null | "needs_template" | "not_supported", default }]; support().listContacts({ customerId?, search?, limit? }) => [{ id, name, identities, customer }] (empty without customerId or search, blocked people left out); uploadAttachment({ ticketId: null, filename, contentType, bytes, uploadedBy }) uploads a file for a ticket that doesn't exist yet, which only its uploader can send. Client: optional startTicket(input) => { ticketId }, listChannels, listContacts, uploadForNewTicket({ file }); with startTicket the inbox shows New ticket and a ticket's customer card shows Message (NewTicketDialog and NewTicketButton in new-ticket-dialog.tsx). With AI, support().ai.draftOpening({ intent, customerId?, contactId?, channelId? }) => { subject, text, sources } drafts the first message from one line and sends nothing (client.ai.draftOpening). Signals: support().signal({ customerId, kind, title, facts?: [{ label, value, url? }], dedupeKey?, to?: { address, name?, locale? } }) => { status: "proposed", outreachId } | { status: "duplicate", outreachId } | { status: "suppressed", reason }. kind is a lowercase letter then lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 60 characters ("incident" is reserved). Checked in order: duplicate (the dedupeKey was reported before, or a proposal of this kind already waits for this customer); recently_contacted (a message of this kind went to the customer within dedupeHours); awaiting_reply (the last one went out within four times dedupeHours, its ticket is still waiting and the customer hasn't written back); dismissed (an agent dismissed this kind for this customer within dedupeHours); customer_limit (maxPerCustomerPerDay proposals or messages in 24 hours across kinds, dismissed ones not counted); rate_limited (maxPerHour signals became proposals in the last hour across customers); no_contact (nobody reachable on a channel that can write first, or the address named is another customer's person or blocked); unavailable (no AI, proactive: false, or the migration isn't applied). The recipient is to, else directory.outreachContact({ customerId, kind }) => { address, name?, locale? } | null (optional), else the person at the customer who wrote last; the language is the contact's locale, else the locale passed, else the language of the customer's recent tickets. The message is drafted (with defer at once, otherwise on the next runScheduled; three attempts) only from the signal's facts, the account facts, the knowledge and approved answers, with sources; when there isn't enough, the proposal waits with no text for an agent to write. Configure with supportAi({ proactive: { dedupeHours: 168, maxPerCustomerPerDay: 2, maxPerHour: 60, minDrafts: 10, minRate: 0.9, windowDays: 90, holdMinutes: 10, maxAutoPerHour: 20, autoSend?: boolean, signature?: false | string | ({ language }) => string } }) or proactive: false. Expose support().ai.listOutreach({ sent? }) (waiting proposals newest first, or with sent the latest sent and dismissed), sendOutreach({ id, actorId, subject?, text? }) => { ticketId } (opens the ticket through startTicket from that agent; two agents sending the same proposal send it once; how much the agent changed is recorded), dismissOutreach({ id, actorId }), holdOutreach({ id, actorId }) (stops a held message), flagOutreach({ id, actorId, note? }) (any agent marks a message that went out on its own as wrong: its kind pauses at once, held messages of the kind return to the queue, the ticket reopens with an outreach_flagged event; deciding on the paused kind is the review), getOutreachKinds() => { autoSend, stopped, minDrafts, minRate, windowDays, holdMinutes, kinds: [{ kind, example, stage: collecting | eligible | on | paused, enabledBy, enabledAt, pausedAt, pauseReason: quality | flagged | null, ready, record }] } and setOutreachKind({ kind, on, actorId }); add the same names to client.ai (the server adds actorId). The inbox shows an Outreach tab when the client has ai.listOutreach (OutreachQueue in outreach.tsx), and SupportAiSettings shows each kind's readiness (OutreachKinds). Sending on its own: nothing does by default. A kind is eligible when at least minRate of its latest minDrafts decided proposals went out as drafted or lightly edited (the same measure as Autopilot); setOutreachKind({ on: true }) is refused until then, records who and when, and goes through autopilot.canManage when set. Once on, each new message of the kind is held for holdMinutes (status "held", sendAt) and sent by runScheduled unless an agent stops, sends or dismisses it, and only if the model set confident, every cited source resolved with at least one that isn't guidance, Autopilot's kill switch (setAutopilot({ stopped: true })) is off and fewer than maxAutoPerHour went out in the last hour; otherwise it waits with autoBlock (stopped, not_confident, unsourced, hourly_cap, held_back). Such a message has no author, an unassigned ticket, and is signed with fromName and "This message was sent automatically. Reply to it and our team will pick it up." A customer's unhappy first answer to a message, and a flag, count against its kind like a rewrite does. A kind whose latest decided proposals fall under minRate pauses, checked on every runScheduled and each time one is drafted; a held message is sent only while its kind is still on. Incident broadcast (after acknowledgeSpike): previewBroadcast({ spikeId }) => { spikeId, topic, channel, recipients: [{ customer, contact, ticket }], skipped: { unlinked, alreadyMessaged, unreachable } } (one person per customer who wrote in about the spike's topic while it lasted; senders not linked to a customer are never written to), draftBroadcast({ spikeId, intent }) => { subject, text, sources } with {name} and {company} in it, and sendBroadcast({ spikeId, subject, text, actorId }) => { recipients, sent, queued, failed }: one ticket per customer from the approving agent, {name} filled with the first name and {company} with the customer's name (a missing one is written around), one message per spike and customer (a unique index, so approving twice sends once), the first 20 sent at once and the rest by the next runScheduled runs. Each spike carries messaged. Add previewBroadcast, draftBroadcast and sendBroadcast to client.ai for "Message customers" on a spike (BroadcastDialog in outreach.tsx). Self-serve: support().portal.ask({ customerId, userId, question, sessionId? }) => { sessionId, kind: "answer", text, sources } | { sessionId, kind: "handoff", reason: cannot_answer | asked_for_human | blocked | limit }, portal.rateAnswer({ customerId, userId, sessionId, helpful }) and portal.escalate({ customerId, userId, email, name, locale?, sessionId, text? }) => { id }. customerId and userId must come from the session, never from the request. It is off until the team switches it on (support().ai.updateSettings({ selfServe: true }), a switch in SupportAiSettings; getSettings returns selfServe); supportAi({ selfServe: false }) removes it; supportAi({ selfServe: { maxPerHour: 20, maxQuestions: 8, quietHours: 24 } }) sets the caps. portal.list() returns ask: true when it is on. Answers come only from the knowledge, approved answers, the asker's own account facts and lookups declared with portal: true (approval "never" only; run and available then get ticket: null and contact: null; up to 6 per answer); an answer is shown only when the model set confident and every cited source resolved, otherwise the result is a hand-off. escalate opens a portal request (the first question as the subject, the latest question or text as the message) with an internal note listing each question, what AI answered, what it drafted but didn't show, and the sources. Guards: account facts and lookups are read for the customerId the server passed; a sessionId only continues a conversation of the same customer and user; a question that reads like an attempt to steer the assistant or reach another account is handed off before any model call; an answer repeating ten words in a row of the guidance is not shown. Add ask, rateAnswer and escalate to the SupportPortalClient: SupportRequests then shows the Ask box (SupportAsk in support-ask.tsx) when list() says ask: true. Deflection: support().ai.insights() gains selfServe: { current, previous }, each { conversations, answered, deflected, escalated, helpful, notHelpful } for conversations started in the period; deflected means answered, not handed off, and either a thumbs-up, or no rating, nothing asked for quietHours and no ticket from that person since the conversation began. Custom ports: SupportStore needs listContacts({ customerId?, userId?, search?, limit }) and insertAttachment accepting ticketId: null; AiStore needs the methods under "Proactive and self-serve" in ai-store.ts; SupportAction.run and available receive ticket: Ticket | null.
10. For email: use a receiving subdomain (e.g. in.acme.com) for the reply address, keep the main mailbox where it is, and copy mail to the receiving address. The Resend adapter needs a Full access API key to read received mail.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs)
- [Installation](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/installation): registry entry, items, tables, monorepos
- [The service](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/service): createSupport options, storage, notifications, methods, errors
- [Your directory](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/directory): identify, searchCustomers, getCustomers, listAgents, describeCustomer, outreachContact, trust
- [Webhooks and scheduling](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/webhooks): the route, responses, runScheduled
- [Inbox and tickets](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/screens): SupportClient, SupportProvider props, New ticket and the Outreach tab, translations
- [Insights](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/insights): SupportInsights, support.stats, how each number is defined, topics and drafts with AI, spikes and insights.spike
- [Customer portal](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/portal): portal.list, get, create and reply, the screens, the Ask box
- [Theming](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/theming)
- [AI](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/ai): supportAi options, providers, knowledge sources, account facts, deferral, client.ai, voice, memory (approved answers, learning from edits, guidance suggestions, gaps, articles), actions (lookups, proposed actions with approval, manual runs, safety), autopilot (track record, eligibility, hold or immediate, the checks a reply passes, flag, automatic pause, kill switch), privacy
- [Proactive and self-serve](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/proactive): startTicket and which channels can write first, support.signal and the Outreach queue (dedupe and limits), kinds that send on their own, incident broadcast, the portal's Ask box (portal.ask, rateAnswer, escalate, lookups with portal: true, safety), deflection in Insights, the 0007_proactive and 0008_outreach_record migrations
- [Email setup](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/email): receiving domains, threading, trimming, automatic mail, authentication
- [Channels](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/channels): resend, microsoft365, gmail, smtp, twilio, whatsapp, telegram, api, and writing your own (/docs/channels/<name>)
- [Upgrading](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/docs/upgrading)
- [Live demo](https://tendkit.softwaresavants.dev/demo)
- [Source](https://github.com/SoftwareSavants/tendkit)
